New Delhi, Oct 20 (IANS) Tesla has scheduled its annual shareholder meeting for December 3, where investors will vote on the re-election of Chief Executive Elon Musk and other directors, along with an advisory resolution on executive compensation and the appointment of the company's auditor.
According to a proxy filing with the US Securities and Exchange Commission, Tesla has nominated Musk, Chair Robyn Denholm and director JB Straubel for new three-year terms on the board.
Shareholders will also be asked to approve, on a non-binding basis, executive compensation for 2025 and ratify PricewaterhouseCoopers as Tesla's independent auditor for the fiscal year ending December 31.
Moreover, the proxy statement disclosed executive compensation attributed to Musk for 2025 of about $158.36 billion, consisting entirely of stock-based awards.
The figure reflects the accounting value assigned to performance-linked equity grants and does not represent cash compensation received by the billionaire entrepreneur.
Tesla said the awards remain contingent on the achievement of specified market capitalisation and operational targets.
The company previously reported in May that Musk's realised compensation for 2025 was zero with none of the 12 tranches tied to the incentive program having been earned.
The equity package comprises roughly 423.7 million restricted shares that vest only after predetermined milestones are met.
In addition, any earned shares are generally subject to a five-year holding requirement, with limited exceptions.
The annual meeting will be held at Tesla's Gigafactory Texas facility in Austin at 3 pm. However, Central Time and will also be accessible online.
Additionally, the filing highlighted several board-level links between Tesla and SpaceX.
However, the proxy statement did not reference any potential merger involving Tesla and SpaceX.
Apart from that, Elon Musk-backed SpaceX is scheduled to announce its third-quarter results on Tuesday after its shares fell nearly 35 per cent from their post-listing high.
This will be the company's second quarterly earnings report since going public in June, following a volatile stretch for the stock.
The stock has dropped around 35 per cent from the record high it hit soon after its debut.

Tesla's 2026 Annual Meeting to Re-Elect Denholm, Musk, and Straubel; Executive Pay and Auditor Ratification on Agenda
sources.text:
On October 19, 2026, Tesla, Inc. submitted a definitive proxy statement (Schedule 14A) to solicit shareholder votes ahead of its 2026 Annual Meeting of Shareholders set for December 3, 2026.
Key Highlights
- Annual meeting date: December 3, 2026, at 3:00 p.m. Central Time, conducted both virtually and in person at Gigafactory Texas, 1 Tesla Road, Austin, Texas 78725.
- Record date: Shareholders of record as of the close of business on October 13, 2026, are eligible to vote.
- Director election: Three Class I directors—Robyn Denholm, Elon Musk, and JB Straubel—are nominated for three-year terms, with the board recommending a vote "FOR EACH COMPANY NOMINEE."
- Executive compensation vote: A non-binding advisory vote on 2025 executive compensation is proposed, with the board recommending a vote "FOR."
- Auditor ratification: Shareholders will vote to ratify PricewaterhouseCoopers LLP as Tesla's independent registered public accounting firm for the fiscal year ending December 31, 2026, with the board recommending a vote "FOR."
- Milestones cited: Tesla surpassed 10 million vehicle deliveries and began Cybercab production at Gigafactory Texas in 2026.
- Retail voting initiative: Tesla highlights its pioneering efforts in providing no-fee, investor-directed voting tools to empower retail shareholders.
Tesla’s 2026 Proxy Statement Details Director Nominations, Executive Pay Advisory, and Corporate Updates
According to Tesla’s filing, the 2026 Annual Meeting will address three key proposals. The first proposal seeks shareholder approval to re-elect Robyn Denholm, Elon Musk, and JB Straubel as Class I directors for three-year terms. The shareholder letter, signed by Denholm as Chair of the Board, praises Musk and Straubel as "two technological visionaries whose leadership has helped make Tesla what it is today," confirming all three nominees for another term.
The second proposal involves a non-binding advisory vote on executive compensation for 2025, described in the filing as a required shareholder advisory vote on the previous fiscal year’s pay. The third proposal requests shareholder ratification of PricewaterhouseCoopers LLP as Tesla’s independent registered public accounting firm for fiscal year ending December 31, 2026. The meeting will be accessible online and in person for a limited number of shareholders at Gigafactory Texas in Austin.
The shareholder letter also outlines recent operational achievements, including the expansion of Tesla’s Robotaxi service to more U.S. cities, record Megapack deployments from Megafactory Shanghai, production of Megapack 3 at Tesla’s Texas Megafactory, launch of the Tesla Semi, unveiling of the Next Gen Roadster, and the initiation of production lines for Optimus. Additionally, the filing references Tesla’s "Terafab initiative," focused on battery and chip manufacturing investments aimed at securing critical component supplies.
Summary of Tesla’s 2026 Annual Meeting Disclosures
Tesla’s definitive proxy statement for its December 3, 2026 annual shareholder meeting includes three board-supported proposals: the election of three Class I directors, a non-binding advisory vote on 2025 executive compensation, and ratification of PricewaterhouseCoopers LLP as the company’s auditor for fiscal year 2026.
